paragraphs: Here's what this whole story hangs on, friend. "As long as he sought the LORD, God gave him success" (2 Chronicles 26:5). Uzziah didn't get strong because he was clever or lucky. He got strong because he kept seeking God, and the Bible says he "was helped tremendously until he became powerful" (2 Chronicles 26:15).

Then the power got loud, and the helping got quiet in his head. "His arrogance led to his own destruction" (2 Chronicles 26:16). I think a man can have towers, cisterns and a huge army and still forget who built the whole thing. That's the trap, friend. Success feels like something you did ALL BY YOURSELF, and I've stood in front of a tray of perfect cookies and thought exactly that.

So here's what I'm taking from this one. Whatever you're good at, keep seeking the LORD, because He's the One who's been helping the whole time. Uzziah rushed out of the temple in the end, and that's a hard place to land (2 Chronicles 26:20). Stay close, stay humble, and when the good things come, hand the credit right back up where it belongs.
